the development and implementation of NIR SRS for tablet analysis.
the development of a spatially-resolved NIR spectroscopic method to detect the presence of local heterogeneity in tablets.
the development of new analytical methods that can be used for the determination of the quality attributes of solid pharmaceutical dosage forms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SRS can detect local heterogeneity in a tablet, while traditional NIR can detect global heterogeneity in a batch.
NIR SRS is a promising technique that provides spatial information that is useful for tablet analysis.
SRS is a powerful tool that can be used for the determination of assay and for the detection of heterogeneity in tablets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SRS technique is a viable alternative to traditional NIR measurement for the analysis of pharmaceutical tablets, and that SRS can be used for the determination of the local heterogeneity of tablets, as well as the detection of abnormal tablets.
NIR spectroscopy can be utilized for the determination of spatial heterogeneity and local composition in tablets, and that SRS provides a more robust analytical tool for tablet analysis.
the SRS measurement can provide additional information that would not be obtainable with the traditional single-point measurement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SRS can be an important tool for the pharmaceutical industry, especially for the determination of assay, and can help to reduce the number of tablets that need to be analyzed for quality control.
SRS can be used to detect and characterize spatial variations in tablet assay and composition, which is a key requirement for in-line, in real-time tablet quality control.
SRS can be used to detect and reject abnormal tablets that may not be detected by traditional single-point spectroscopy.
